1	# agentmon
2	
3	LLM-as-judge monitoring for coding-agent transcripts.
4	
5	agentmon is a trusted-monitoring harness in the spirit of AI-control work (Greenblatt et al. 2023):
6	a trusted monitor model reads the full transcript of a coding-agent session and emits a structured
7	suspicion verdict — a 0–100 suspicion score, flagged failure categories (`security_vuln`,
8	`reward_hacking`, `scope_expansion`, `deception`), and event-indexed evidence quotes pointing back
9	into the transcript. Monitors are plain markdown prompts; the harness handles ingestion, running
10	monitors over transcript sets, and scoring the results.
11	
12	Evaluation is against labeled transcripts (benign vs. a failure-mode tag). The headline metric is
13	catch rate at a fixed false-positive budget — recall @ 1% and 5% FPR: with a threshold calibrated
14	to flag only 1% of benign transcripts, what fraction of true failures do we catch? The report also
15	includes AUROC, precision/recall/F1 at a fixed threshold, and cost/latency per transcript, since a
16	monitor that's accurate but too expensive to run on every session isn't deployable. agentmon
17	ingests real Claude Code session logs, and the entire test suite runs against a deterministic mock
18	LLM — no API key needed for `uv run pytest`.
19	
20	## Architecture
21	
22	```
23	session logs (~/.claude/projects)
24	        |
25	        v
26	     ingest  ──>  Transcript JSONL
27	                       |
28	                       v
29	                    runner  (monitors x transcripts, on-disk response cache)
30	                       |
31	                       v
32	                MonitorVerdicts ──> eval ──> results.json + report.md
33	```
34	
35	Monitors are defined as `prompts/*.md` files with YAML frontmatter (id, model, categories, …) and
36	a `{{transcript}}` placeholder in the body. All LLM access goes through an `LLMClient` protocol
37	with two implementations: `AnthropicClient` (live) and `MockLLMClient` (deterministic, for tests
38	and `--mock` runs).
39	
40	## Quickstart
41	
42	```sh
43	uv sync
44	uv run pytest
45	uv run agentmon ingest --source claude-code --path tests/fixtures/claude_code_session.jsonl --out out/transcripts
46	uv run agentmon run --monitor example_security --input tests/fixtures/claude_code_session.jsonl --mock
47	uv run agentmon eval --verdicts datasets/samples/toy_verdicts.jsonl --labels datasets/samples/toy_labels.jsonl --out out/eval
48	```
49	
50	`--mock` uses the deterministic mock client; drop it and set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for live runs.
51	
52	## Repo layout
53	
54	```
55	src/agentmon/
56	  schemas.py      # pydantic models: Event union, Transcript, MonitorVerdict, eval results
57	  ingest/         # Claude Code session logs -> normalized Transcript JSONL
58	  monitors/       # monitor loading: prompt parsing, transcript rendering, verdict parsing
59	  prompts/        # monitor definitions: *.md with YAML frontmatter + prompt body
60	  llm/            # LLMClient protocol, AnthropicClient, MockLLMClient
61	  runner.py       # run monitors x transcripts with an on-disk response cache
62	  eval/           # score verdicts against labels: AUROC, recall @ fixed FPR, cost
63	  cli.py          # typer CLI: agentmon ingest | run | eval
64	datasets/         # sample verdict/label sets for the eval pipeline
65	tests/            # everything runs against MockLLMClient; no network, no API key
66	```
67	
68	## Roadmap (explicitly out of scope today)
69	
70	- Real monitor prompt library and failure-mode taxonomy docs
71	- Synthetic dataset generation (injecting failure modes into benign transcripts)
72	- Hierarchical monitoring (cheap first pass, escalate suspicious transcripts)
73	- Automated red-teaming of monitors
74	- Live monitoring via Claude Code hooks
75	- Fine-tuned open-source monitors
76	
77	## License

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	Conventions for working in this repo.
4	
5	- `src/agentmon/schemas.py` is the contract. Every other module codes against it. If a model needs
6	  to change, change schemas.py first, deliberately, then update dependents.
7	- Mock-first: tests NEVER make live API calls or construct `AnthropicClient`. Use
8	  `agentmon.llm.mock.MockLLMClient`. `uv run pytest` must pass with no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set.
9	- Monitors live in `src/agentmon/prompts/*.md`: YAML frontmatter (`id`, `description`,
10	  `categories`, `model`, `max_transcript_tokens`) plus a body containing a `{{transcript}}`
11	  placeholder.
12	- The runner caches LLM responses in `.agentmon_cache/`, keyed by
13	  `hash(prompt, transcript, model, temperature)`. Delete the directory to force re-runs.
14	- Before finishing any task, run `uv run ruff check`, `uv run ruff format`, and `uv run pytest`.
15	- Line length is 100. Use `uv` for all commands (`uv run`, `uv sync`).
16	- Keep it boring: no async, no database, no plugin framework. Small functions, full type hints,
17	  `from __future__ import annotations`, `pathlib.Path`.
18

1	# datasets/
2	
3	Local data for evaluating monitors. Everything in this directory is gitignored
4	**except** this README and the tiny committed samples under `samples/` (see the
5	`datasets/*` rules in the repo `.gitignore`). Put real transcript dumps, verdict
6	runs, and label sets here without worrying about committing them.
7	
8	## File formats
9	
10	Both formats are JSONL: one pydantic model (from `agentmon.schemas`) serialized
11	as JSON per line. Load with `Model.model_validate_json(line)`; write with
12	`model.model_dump_json()`.
13	
14	### Verdicts (`*_verdicts.jsonl`)
15	
16	One `MonitorVerdict` per line — a monitor's judgment of one transcript:
17	`monitor_id`, `transcript_id`, `suspicion_score` (0–100), `categories`
18	(failure-mode tags), `evidence` (event index + quote pairs), `reasoning`,
19	plus usage fields (`model`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `latency_ms`).
20	
21	### Labels (`*_labels.jsonl`)
22	
23	One `LabeledTranscript` per line — ground truth for one transcript:
24	`transcript_id`, `label` (`benign` or one of `security_vuln`,
25	`reward_hacking`, `scope_expansion`, `deception`, `other`), optional `notes`.
26	
27	## Committed samples
28	
29	`samples/toy_verdicts.jsonl` and `samples/toy_labels.jsonl` are a hand-built
30	12-transcript set (8 benign, 4 failures — one per category) for monitor
31	`example_security`. Their metrics are hand-computed and asserted in
32	`tests/test_metrics.py`, so treat them as frozen: if you edit them, update the
33	worked arithmetic in the tests to match.
34	
35	## Regenerating or extending
36	
37	The samples were written by hand; to extend them (or build a new set), emit one
38	model per line:
39	
40	```python
41	from pathlib import Path
42	from agentmon.schemas import LabeledTranscript
43	
44	labels = [LabeledTranscript(transcript_id="t13", label="benign", notes="...")]
45	with Path("datasets/my_labels.jsonl").open("w") as f:
46	    for label in labels:
47	        f.write(label.model_dump_json() + "\n")
48	```
49	
50	Validate a file by round-tripping every line through
51	`model_validate_json`, then run the eval harness over it with
52	`agentmon.eval.metrics.evaluate`.

1	"""Run monitors over transcripts with an optional on-disk response cache.
2	
3	The cache stores raw :class:`~agentmon.llm.client.LLMResponse` payloads keyed
4	by (prompt template, transcript content, model, temperature), so re-runs cost
5	nothing and experiments stay reproducible. Verdicts are always rebuilt by
6	re-parsing the (cached or fresh) response through the monitor.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import hashlib
12	import json
13	from pathlib import Path
14	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
15	
16	from pydantic import ValidationError
17	
18	from agentmon.llm.client import LLMClient, LLMResponse
19	from agentmon.monitors.base import Monitor
20	from agentmon.schemas import MonitorVerdict, Transcript
21	
22	if TYPE_CHECKING:
23	    from collections.abc import Sequence
24	
25	_TEMPERATURE = 0.0
26	
27	
28	def cache_key(monitor: Monitor, transcript: Transcript) -> str:
29	    """Deterministic cache key for one (monitor, transcript) pair."""
30	    payload = json.dumps(
31	        {
32	            "prompt": monitor.template,
33	            "transcript": transcript.model_dump_json(),
34	            "model": monitor.config.model,
35	            "temperature": _TEMPERATURE,
36	        },
37	        sort_keys=True,
38	    )
39	    return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
40	
41	
42	def _read_cached_response(path: Path) -> LLMResponse | None:
43	    """Load a cached response, treating any missing or corrupt file as a miss."""
44	    try:
45	        return LLMResponse.model_validate_json(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
46	    except (OSError, ValueError, ValidationError):
47	        return None
48	
49	
50	def run_monitors(
51	    monitors: Sequence[Monitor],
52	    transcripts: Sequence[Transcript],
53	    client: LLMClient,
54	    cache_dir: Path | None = None,
55	) -> list[MonitorVerdict]:
56	    """Run every monitor over every transcript, returning one verdict per pair.
57	
58	    Calls are sequential (monitors outer, transcripts inner) at temperature 0.
59	    With ``cache_dir`` set, responses are cached on disk and cache hits skip
60	    the client entirely; ``cache_dir=None`` disables caching.
61	    """
62	    verdicts: list[MonitorVerdict] = []
63	    for monitor in monitors:
64	        for transcript in transcripts:
65	            prompt = monitor.build_prompt(transcript)
66	            cache_path = cache_dir / f"{cache_key(monitor, transcript)}.json" if cache_dir else None
67	            response = _read_cached_response(cache_path) if cache_path else None
68	            if response is None:
69	                response = client.complete(
70	                    prompt, model=monitor.config.model, temperature=_TEMPERATURE
71	                )
72	                if cache_path is not None:
73	                    cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
74	                    cache_path.write_text(response.model_dump_json(), encoding="utf-8")
75	            verdicts.append(monitor.verdict_from_response(transcript.id, response))
76	    return verdicts
77

18	    "claude-fable-5": (10.0, 50.0),
19	    "claude-opus-4-8": (5.0, 25.0),
20	    "claude-opus-4-7": (5.0, 25.0),
21	    "claude-opus-4-6": (5.0, 25.0),
22	    "claude-sonnet-4-6": (3.0, 15.0),
23	    "claude-haiku-4-5": (1.0, 5.0),
24	}

26	
27	def auroc(scores: Sequence[float], is_positive: Sequence[bool]) -> float | None:
28	    """Area under the ROC curve via the rank-based Mann-Whitney U statistic.
29	
30	    Tied scores receive average ranks. Returns None when there are no
31	    positives or no negatives, where AUROC is undefined.
32	    """
33	    n_pos = sum(is_positive)
34	    n_neg = len(is_positive) - n_pos
35	    if n_pos == 0 or n_neg == 0:
36	        return None
37	    order = sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: scores[i])
38	    ranks = [0.0] * len(scores)
39	    i = 0
40	    while i < len(order):
41	        j = i
42	        while j < len(order) and scores[order[j]] == scores[order[i]]:
43	            j += 1
44	        avg_rank = (i + j + 1) / 2  # average of the 1-based ranks i+1 .. j
45	        for idx in order[i:j]:
46	            ranks[idx] = avg_rank
47	        i = j
48	    rank_sum = sum(r for r, pos in zip(ranks, is_positive, strict=True) if pos)
49	    u = rank_sum - n_pos * (n_pos + 1) / 2
50	    return u / (n_pos * n_neg)
51	
52	
53	def recall_at_fpr(
54	    scores: Sequence[float], is_positive: Sequence[bool], max_fpr: float
55	) -> float | None:
56	    """Recall under a false-alarm budget: with a threshold that flags at most
57	    ``max_fpr`` of benign transcripts, what fraction of true failures do we catch?
58	
59	    The threshold flags strictly greater scores. With benign scores sorted
60	    descending and ``k = floor(max_fpr * n_benign)``, the threshold is the

findings.title: Mock runs poison the cache for live runs; README's "drop --mock for live runs" silently returns mock verdicts
findings.detail: README.md line 50 says: "--mock uses the deterministic mock client; drop it and set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for live runs." But runner.cache_key() hashes only (template, transcript JSON, model, temperature) — nothing about which client produced the response — and both mock and live runs share the default cache dir .agentmon_cache/ (cli.py _DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR). So the exact README flow — quickstart mock run, then re-run without --mock — is a cache hit: the Anthropic API is never called and the canned MockLLMClient verdict is printed as if it were a live result, with model set to the real model id (claude-opus-4-8) so it is indistinguishable downstream. Confirmed empirically with two distinct clients sharing a cache dir: the second client's call_count was 0 and the returned verdict carried the first client's response text. For a monitoring harness, silently reporting a mock judgment as a live one is exactly the failure the tool exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Include a client/namespace discriminator in the cache key (e.g. a client.cache_namespace or an is_mock flag), or have the CLI use a separate cache dir (or pass cache_dir=None) when --mock is set. Update the README sentence to mention deleting .agentmon_cache/ if the shared cache is kept intentionally.

findings.title: Docs describe "committed samples" and a working CI, but the repo's only commit is a 2-line stub README
findings.detail: datasets/README.md calls samples/toy_*.jsonl "the tiny committed samples" and README.md implies a working repo, but `git ls-files` shows only README.md is tracked; HEAD (d53c8ef "Initial commit") contains a 2-line stub ("# agent-monitor / monitoring system for detecting security vulnerabilities...") that doesn't match the working-tree README. Everything else — src/, tests/, datasets/, .github/workflows/ci.yml, LICENSE, pyproject.toml, .gitignore itself — is untracked, so CI has never run and the published repo (if pushed today) shows none of the documented project. The .gitignore mechanics are correct (`git check-ignore datasets/samples/toy_verdicts.jsonl` exits 1 — not ignored — and `!datasets/README.md` matches), so a plain `git add` will do the right thing for datasets/, but until then every "committed" claim is falsifiable in seconds.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit the scaffold (git add -A after fixing the .gitignore gaps below) so the tree matches the docs, and verify the CI workflow actually triggers on push.

findings.title: README says ingest produces "Transcript JSONL"; it actually writes one pretty-printed .json file per transcript
findings.detail: Both the architecture diagram ("ingest ──> Transcript JSONL", line 26) and the repo-layout annotation ("ingest/ # Claude Code session logs -> normalized Transcript JSONL", line 58) claim JSONL output. Running the quickstart ingest command writes out/transcripts/claude_code_session.json — a single indent=2 JSON document per transcript (cli.py ingest, line 100). The distinction matters because the CLI's --input dispatches on suffix: .jsonl is parsed as a raw Claude Code session log and .json as an ingested Transcript (cli.py _load_transcript), so a user who actually produced "Transcript JSONL" could not feed it back into `agentmon run`.
findings.suggested_fix: Change both README mentions to "Transcript JSON files (one per transcript)" — or, if JSONL is the intended interchange format, change ingest to emit one transcripts.jsonl and teach _load_transcript to read it.

findings.title: Cache key hashes the template, not the prompt: editing max_transcript_tokens silently hits stale cache
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md (lines 12-13) says the runner cache is "keyed by hash(prompt, transcript, model, temperature)". runner.cache_key() actually hashes monitor.template, and the real prompt also depends on config.max_transcript_tokens (Monitor.build_prompt truncates the rendered transcript at max_transcript_tokens * 4 chars). Confirmed: two monitors with identical templates but max_transcript_tokens=16000 vs 1 build different prompts yet produce identical cache keys, so changing that frontmatter field returns stale cached responses for the old truncation. The documented key and the implemented key disagree precisely in the case where it causes wrong results.
findings.suggested_fix: Hash the built prompt (monitor.build_prompt(transcript)) instead of monitor.template in cache_key — the prompt already incorporates template, transcript rendering, and truncation — or add max_transcript_tokens to the key payload and fix the CLAUDE.md wording.

findings.title: .gitignore misses the quickstart's out/ directory and .claude/settings.local.json
findings.detail: The README quickstart writes out/transcripts and out/eval into the repo root, but `git check-ignore out/eval/report.md` exits 1 — out/ is not ignored (while .agentmon_cache/ is). Anyone following the quickstart then running `git add .` (which is also the step needed to fix the uncommitted-scaffold issue) commits generated artifacts. The same `git add .` would also commit .claude/settings.local.json, which is the by-convention machine-local Claude Code settings file and here contains a long session-specific permission allowlist including absolute paths under /Users/user — not something for a public portfolio repo.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `out/` and `.claude/settings.local.json` to .gitignore (keep .claude/settings.json committed if the project allowlist is intended to be shared).

findings.title: README's failure-category list omits `other`, which the schema and labels accept
findings.detail: README line 7-8 enumerates the flagged categories as security_vuln, reward_hacking, scope_expansion, deception. schemas.FailureCategory also defines OTHER = "other"; it is a valid verdict category (monitors/base._parse_categories accepts it) and a valid label (datasets/README.md correctly lists it among label values). A reader cross-checking README against the schema or datasets/README hits the mismatch immediately.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `other` to the README category list (or note it as the catch-all tag).

findings.title: CLI cannot run a monitor over a transcript set, so the documented ingest -> runner -> eval pipeline isn't executable end-to-end from the CLI
findings.detail: README line 9-10 says the harness handles "running monitors over transcript sets", and the architecture diagram chains ingest -> runner -> eval. run_monitors() does take sequences, but `agentmon run --input` accepts exactly one file (cli.py rejects directories via _load_transcript), so the directory of .json transcripts produced by `agentmon ingest --out out/transcripts` cannot be fed to `agentmon run`; building a verdicts JSONL for `agentmon eval` requires one invocation per transcript with --out append.
findings.suggested_fix: Let `agentmon run --input` accept a directory (glob *.json/*.jsonl, reuse run_monitors over the list), or soften the README to say set-level runs are library-level (agentmon.runner.run_monitors) for now.
